name: com.oooworks/free-tools
title: OOO Works free tools
description: Can ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI and Copilot read a web page? Free check, no sign-in.

tools.name: check_ai_booking
tools.description: Reads a business's homepage and up to four of its booking, menu or price pages, finds the booking or ordering tools it links to or embeds (OpenTable, Resy, Booksy, Fresha, Vagaro, Square, Jobber and about 35 others), and says for Google AI Mode, Google's Book button, ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity whether they can book or order through those tools (yes, no or unclear, with the source of each yes and the countries it applies to). Also says whether prices are on the site, since Google's AI may phone a business to ask. Only sees the website. Limited to 30 checks an hour per caller (shared with the other checks); results are cached for 10 minutes.

url.description: the website or page, e.g. example.com or https://example.com/page

tools.name: check_ai_crawler_access
tools.description: Checks one web page: robots.txt rules for each AI crawler (search, user and training crawlers kept apart), what the server returns to each crawler's name compared with a normal browser and a plain automated request, noindex, and whether llms.txt is well formed. Returns one line per assistant (ok, blocked, or unknown when the site verifies real crawlers by IP), fixes, robots.txt lines to paste, and notes. Limited to 30 checks an hour per caller; results are cached for 10 minutes.

url.description: the website or page to check, e.g. example.com or https://example.com/page

tools.name: check_email_security
tools.description: Looks up a domain's public DNS: SPF (one record, how it ends, an estimate of its DNS lookups against the limit of 10), DMARC (policy none, quarantine or reject, and whether reports are sent), MX (and the mail provider when recognisable), and DKIM keys under common selector names (google, selector1/selector2, k1, s1/s2, default, resend and others). A DKIM key that isn't found under those names isn't necessarily missing. Returns findings with plain-word fixes and DNS records to copy (a starter DMARC with p=none, the next step to p=quarantine). Reads DNS only; it can't see whether mail actually passes. Limited to 30 checks an hour per caller (shared with the other checks); results are cached for 10 minutes.

domain.description: the email domain, e.g. example.com (an email address or website address works too)

tools.name: check_site_health
tools.description: One look at a site from outside: whether the home page answers and how fast (one sample, not monitoring), the TLS certificate (issuer, days left, the names it covers, protocol, TLS 1.0/1.1), the domain's registration expiry from the registry's RDAP service (unknown when the registry doesn't publish it), email authentication (SPF, DMARC, MX, DKIM under common selectors), security headers graded A to F (HSTS, CSP, nosniff, framing, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), cookies and tracking scripts on first load, a recognised cookie banner and a privacy policy link, http to https forwarding and mixed content. Findings come with plain-word fixes. Not legal advice and not a compliance check. Limited to 30 checks an hour per caller (shared with the other checks); results are cached for 10 minutes.

url.description: the website or page, e.g. example.com or https://example.com/page

tools.name: check_sitemap
tools.description: Finds a site's XML sitemap (robots.txt Sitemap lines, /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /wp-sitemap.xml, or the sitemap address given), checks it against the sitemaps.org protocol (valid XML, root and namespace, at most 50,000 addresses and 50 MB, full addresses on the same host, lastmod dates), follows a sitemap index to at most 5 sitemaps, and opens up to 20 listed addresses to find errors, redirects, noindex and canonical tags pointing elsewhere. Returns findings with plain-word fixes. Limited to 30 checks an hour per caller (shared with the other checks); results are cached for 10 minutes.

url.description: the website or page, e.g. example.com or https://example.com/page

tools.name: check_social_search_preview
tools.description: Reads one web page and estimates how it appears as a Google result (title and description, with where they're likely cut off: an estimate, since Google cuts by width and often rewrites them) and as a link preview (Open Graph and X card tags, and the preview image's status, type and pixel size). Returns findings with plain-word fixes. Limited to 30 checks an hour per caller (shared with the other checks); results are cached for 10 minutes.

url.description: the website or page, e.g. example.com or https://example.com/page

tools.name: draft_faq_page
tools.description: Reads a business's website (the home page and up to 8 more pages of the same site, honouring robots.txt) and drafts up to 12 questions its customers would ask, each answered only from text on one of those pages, with the page's address and the words quoted from it. Gemini drafts them without web search; then OOO Works' checks drop any answer whose quote isn't on the cited page word for word, or that has a number, price, time, phone number, link or boast that isn't on that page. Questions the site doesn't answer are listed separately, as what to add. Returns the FAQ, an HTML block and FAQPage JSON-LD to paste. Nothing is changed on the site. Limited to 5 a day per caller; a site is read at most once a day and the same site and language are answered from memory for 24 hours.

url.description: the business's website, e.g. example.com; its home page and up to 8 more pages of the same site are read

language.description: language to write the FAQ in: en (default) or ko

tools.name: get_ai_ready_badge
tools.description: Returns what the OOO Works AI-ready badge says for a site (can read, partly, blocked, can't test, or not checked), when it was checked, and the HTML to show the badge. Read-only: it never starts a check. The badge reflects OOO Works' check of robots.txt and the server's answers to each AI crawler's name at that time; it isn't a certification. For a fresh result, run check_ai_crawler_access on the site's homepage.

host.description: the website's host name, e.g. example.com

tools.name: get_review_insights
tools.description: Reads 5 to 60 customer reviews of one business (from Google, Naver, Yelp or anywhere, any language) and returns the top 3 things customers love, the top 3 things they complain about, up to 3 fixes each tied to a complaint, and one strength to use in marketing. Gemini reads the reviews only, without web search; reviewer names and profile lines are removed first. Then OOO Works' checks keep only quotes found word for word in the reviews, count each theme as the number of reviews with such a quote, and drop anything with a reviewer's name, contact details or a number not in the reviews, and any fix that ties a reward to reviews. Themes and fixes are in English or Korean (lang); quotes stay as written. Reviews aren't stored. Limited to 5 runs a day per caller; identical requests are answered from memory for 24 hours.

reviews.description: the customer reviews, one per item, 5 to 60, any language, at most 2,000 characters each and 30,000 in all

business_type.description: what the business does, e.g. cafe or dentist; helps the fixes fit

lang.description: language of the themes, fixes and notes: en (default) or ko; quotes stay in the reviews' language

tools.name: write_review_reply
tools.description: Writes up to three reply drafts (short, warm, formal; at most 120 words each) that a business owner can post under a customer review on Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Naver or elsewhere. Gemini writes them from the review and the owner's details only, without web search; then OOO Works' checks drop any draft that offers or promises something the owner didn't (refunds, discounts, free items, guarantees), asks for the review to be changed or removed, adds a number, name, link or phone number that isn't in the review or the owner's details, makes a superlative or health claim, or, for a health business, mentions any health detail. Warnings say what to watch before posting. Drafts are suggestions for the owner to read and edit; nothing is posted. Limited to 10 replies a day per caller; identical requests are answered from memory for 24 hours.

business_type.description: what the business does, e.g. dentist or Italian restaurant

review.description: the customer's review as posted, at most 2,000 characters

stars.description: the review's star rating, 1 to 5; leave out when there is none

platform.description: where it was posted: google, yelp, tripadvisor, naver, kakao, facebook, trustpilot, booking, airbnb or other

language.description: reply language: auto (the review's language), en, ko, ja, zh, es, fr, de, it, pt, nl, vi, th or id

reviewer.description: the reviewer's name as the platform shows it, to greet them by

contact.description: phone, email or page where the reviewer can reach the business privately

what_to_say.description: anything the owner wants the reply to say, in their words

tools.name: write_social_posts
tools.description: Reads a small business's website (the home page and up to 6 pages on the same site) and writes five social media posts for the week, Monday to Friday: a service spotlight, behind the scenes, a question answered, a tip and a gentle call to action. Each has a caption, 3 to 6 hashtags, an idea for a photo the owner can take, and the page it's based on. Gemini writes them from the site's text only, without web search; then OOO Works' checks drop any post with a number, offer, discount, price, award or other claim that isn't on its page, a quote or talk of reviews, or a link to another site. Posts can be shaped for Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads, X, Naver Blog or a KakaoTalk channel, in English or Korean. Nothing is posted; the owner reads and posts them. Limited to 5 runs a day per caller; the same site and choices are answered from memory for 24 hours.

platform.description: where the posts go: any, instagram, facebook, linkedin, threads, x, naver-blog or kakao-channel (default any)
